svg.title: opusfleet on AWS — reference architecture
svg.text: Reference architecture for deploying the audio-device service: cellular Opus ingest, a managed event bus, durable segments, an inference lane, and the platform around it.
X.509 key in a secure element
firmware pins a numeric IP — this keeps it stable
terminates device TLS and the CMS origin
X.509 per device, OTA jobs, STAT telemetry
keeps traffic off the public internet
never decodes audio; the only task
that must keep up in real time
levels is the decode stage — the only
one that scales with fleet size
the single biggest cost lever at fleet scale
decouples the inference lane from ingest
fans a finished segment out to the models below
the gap in the current design —
GitHub Actions assumes a role via
build → scan → push → ECS rolling deploy
Alarm on consumer lag, not CPU —
lag is what actually signals falling behind
the thing a single-process server never gave you
SSE-KMS on the bucket, TLS in transit,
replaces plaintext keys in a file
registered in the IoT Core registry
Today a device is trusted purely because it
said HELLO:<imei> — anyone can claim any id.
